5.1.5 looks like validation to me. It's typically called "allow list validation" and this kind of validation does in fact almost always provide a needed security benefit when protecting redirects. 

5.1.6 is just doing a size limit check, a form of validation.  Depending on the underlying framework, a programmer doing this manually may or may not provide a major security benefit. 

But these both seem like security validation to me.

2 more changes:
* changed "cookie header" > "cookie header field"
* change "results in the server returning an error message" > "results the server always responds with an error status such as 400 or 431" 
* removed "until cookies are manually cleared" - how to get rid of them is not in the scope of this requirement. If the cookie is wihtout an expire time set (called a session cookie), it is removed when browser close->reopen. Technically you can also do cookie cleanup via `Clear-Site-Data` (see requirement 8.2.3).
